But then after the 500 error on the mobilitaet/gebaeude/klima pages, `/` also started returning 500 with wachstum-recent.csv not being found.

This is a known behavior in Next.js's dev mode: when a compilation error occurs in one of the page routes, the webpack module graph gets contaminated — actually, more precisely, in Next.js dev, when a shared module that is part of the shared chunks (e.g., a client or server component that's part of the shared manifest) has a compile error, the compilation error state can propagate to other routes that share modules. In practice, Next.js dev has a known behavior where a compile failure on any page can invalidate the build of other pages, especially in the case of client-side navigation or shared chunks.

Actually, there's a known Next.js issue: when a shared module (e.g., a module included in the server entry of multiple pages) has a compile error, webpack's "notFound" state gets cached in the in-memory compilation, and subsequent page requests that reference the same shared module also fail.

This is plausible: a webpack build failure for a module in a shared chunk invalidates the entire shared chunk, and all pages that use it fail.
